question: Five years ago, the ratio of the ages of two buildings was 7 : 2. Five years hence, the ratio will be 3 : 1. What is the present age of the newer building?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio 5 yrs ago = 7 : 2 (diff 5) | Ratio 5 yrs hence = 3 : 1 (diff 2)

Equalize difference: (7:2) × 2 = 14 : 4 and (3:1) × 5 = 15 : 5

Increase of 1 unit (15−14 or 5−4) = 10 years (5 years ago to 5 years hence)

Newer building age 5 years ago = 4 units = 4 × 10 = 40 years

Present age = 40 + 5 = 45 years

**∴ The correct answer is 45 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio 5 years ago = 7 : 2

Ratio 5 years hence = 3 : 1

**Formula Used:**

Age = Ratio value × Constant factor (x)
